clue.text: Simple sound heard by rugby player

indicators.note: something heard is taken in by ear, so the word for sound is wanted as it is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: a sound is a narrow channel of sea, a strait; said out loud it matches a word for direct
a forward is a pack player in rugby, as opposed to a back

explanation.surface: Someone hears a simple noise coming from a rugby player on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a noise but is the sea channel, a strait; STRAIGHT plus FORWARD makes STRAIGHTFORWARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something straightforward is uncomplicated and easy to understand, a plain synonym for simple.

clue.text: Hugely value firm before August news article about debt banks ignored

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its outside letters, so ignoring them keeps only the inner part
about means surrounding, so the article wraps around the other letters
before places one piece ahead of the next in the answer

blocks.note: set means firm or solid, as a jelly sets
august means grand or eminent
a journalist's piece is a story
the word debt with its first and last letters dropped

explanation.surface: A firm prepares a news story about a debt ahead of an August deadline, ignoring the banks.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on August disguises the adjective meaning grand or majestic, and 'banks' are a word's outer letters, not lenders.
explanation.definitionFit: To set great store by something is an idiom meaning to regard it as very important or prize it highly.

clue.text: Class of Oxford scholars announced courses

indicators.note: something announced is spoken aloud, so the scholars' name is wanted for its pronunciation

blocks.note: Rhodes scholars are a famous class of overseas students funded to study at Oxford

explanation.surface: A group of Oxford students has its course list read out.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhodes Scholarships bring international students to Oxford University; Rhodes and ROADS sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Roads are routes or ways along which one travels, which is one sense of courses.

clue.text: EMI cutting its electronic record

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the first word goes inside the next one

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; EMI is a British record company
E is the standard abbreviation for electronic, as in email

explanation.surface: The record label EMI trims costs on its electronic music release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' sits naturally beside the record company EMI but is the verb meaning to list in detail.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to set down every item separately in a list, so to record things one by one.

clue.text: Selfie wearing stockings in nursing home

indicators.note: one thing wearing another has it on, so the photo is inside the stockings word

blocks.note: hose is an old general word for stockings and tights
a selfie is a photo, informally a pic

explanation.surface: Someone takes a photo of themselves in stockings inside a care home.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospice is a home providing care for the terminally ill, so a kind of nursing home.

clue.text: They might be worn out playing 2 iron at the outset

indicators.note: out playing suggests letters loose and disordered, so they are rearranged
at the outset puts the metal symbol right at the start of the answer

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
2 refers to the answer of 2 down

explanation.surface: Golfers playing a 2 iron off the tee wear something out.
explanation.walkthrough: The '2 iron' is a golf club in the surface, but 2 points to the answer of 2 down and iron is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Fedoras are soft felt hats, and hats are examples of things that might be worn on the head.

clue.text: Theatre student interrupting benefit in disgust

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so the student letter goes inside the benefit word

blocks.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
use means benefit or advantage, as in of no use
L is a learner driver, a student

explanation.surface: A drama student breaks up a charity benefit performance and everyone is appalled.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse is to cause strong revulsion or aversion, so to fill someone with loathing; a verb sense.

clue.text: Fancy a tipple – name one cocktail

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine or dress up, so these letters are made into something new

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A barman asks a customer whether they would like a drink and to name one cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy a tipple' reads as a friendly offer of a drink, but Fancy is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An appletini is a vodka martini flavoured with apple liqueur, an example of a mixed drink.

clue.text: Awful Everton on edge defending headers from Tottenham Hotspur – that’s a touchy subject!

indicators.note: headers are the heads of the words, so only their opening letters are taken
awful means terrible and in bad shape, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letters of the two words of the club name

explanation.surface: A nervous Everton side defends badly against Tottenham, and their fans would rather not discuss it.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton and Tottenham Hotspur are English Premier League football clubs; the two initials are held inside the other letters before everything is mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Don't even go there is a colloquial warning to avoid raising a sore or sensitive topic.

clue.text: Went through part of song in jazz style

indicators.note: in places the song part inside the jazz style word

blocks.note: trad is traditional jazz, the revivalist New Orleans style
a verse is a section of a song

explanation.surface: A singer went through a verse of a song arranged in a jazz style.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across or pass over, so went through a place is its past tense.

clue.text: Call by parrot – less noisy bird

indicators.note: less means minus, so the bird is taken away from the longer word

blocks.note: popinjay is an old word for a parrot
the jay is a crow family bird known for its harsh screech

explanation.surface: A parrot pays a call, quieter than some other noisy bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less noisy' looks like quieter, but less is the minus sign and noisy describes the bird removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop in is a casual phrasal verb meaning to make a brief informal visit to someone.

clue.text: Tell composer Fellini’s sorry about cutting bits

indicators.note: cutting bits means slicing letters out of the words, so the answer is a run within them
about means turned round, so the run is read backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters from the end of the director's name through the start of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone tells a composer that Fellini apologises for cutting parts from a film.
explanation.walkthrough: Tell is not a verb here: it is William Tell, the opera whose overture is famous.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossini wrote the opera William Tell, so he is the composer of Tell.

clue.text: On reflection always assuming priest provides comfort

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the other way round, so the word is read backwards
assuming means taking on, so the priest is taken inside

blocks.note: ever means always
Eli is the biblical priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A priest, thinking it over, always offers comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the stock crossword priest from the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve is to ease pain or distress, and comfort as a verb means to soothe in the same way.

clue.text: Holiday home let out before tea dance

indicators.note: let out tells us to leave out the word let itself from the holiday home
before places the first piece ahead of the second

blocks.note: a chalet is a holiday cabin
taken as written and removed
cha or char is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A holiday cottage is rented out ahead of a tea dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let out' reads as renting the home, but it means take LET out of CHALET.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha is a lively Latin American ballroom dance of Cuban origin.

clue.text: Gradually build up – for beginners climbing Cuillin Ridge is bracing

indicators.note: beginners are the opening letters, so only the first of each word is used
bracing means holding firm on each side, so the ridge clasps the letters

blocks.note: the first letters of the two words
an arete is a sharp mountain ridge

explanation.surface: Novice climbers find the Cuillin Ridge invigorating and build up their skills gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cuillin are mountains on the Isle of Skye in Scotland. 'Bracing' looks like invigorating but is the container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrete is to grow by slow accumulation of layers or particles over time.

clue.text: PM once in hotel guarded by dog, unfriendly

indicators.note: something guarded by another is surrounded by it, so the hotel letter goes inside

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
chill means cold and unwelcoming

explanation.surface: A former prime minister is in a hotel, guarded by an unfriendly dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Churchill was famously compared to a bulldog, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill was Britain's wartime Prime Minister, a past holder of that office.

clue.text: Articulated food truck, oddly, a three-wheeler

indicators.note: articulated means pronounced clearly, so the word is wanted for its sound
oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters only

blocks.note: tuck is British school slang for food and snacks
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: An articulated food truck turns out, strangely, to have only three wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulated' belongs with truck in the surface, a lorry with a hinged trailer, but it signals speech here.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuk-tuk is a motorised rickshaw with three wheels, common as a taxi in South and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Step to keep emergency room germ-free

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the step word holds the other letters

blocks.note: a stile is a step for climbing over a fence
ER is the abbreviation for emergency room

explanation.surface: A procedure for keeping a hospital emergency department clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile means free from bacteria and other living microorganisms, so germ-free is a direct synonym.

clue.text: See 16
Sounds of mice and rats

blocks.note: first meaning: the high-pitched cries rodents make
second meaning: informs, as a verb; squeak is slang for informing on someone

explanation.walkthrough: Mice and rats look like a pair of rodents, but rats is a verb meaning grasses or tells on.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeaks are thin shrill noises, and to squeak is also slang for to inform on a person.

clue.text: Old Austin‘s somewhat abysmal legroom

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of, so the answer is a portion of the following words

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A complaint that an old car had terrible space for the legs.
explanation.walkthrough: The Allegro was a 1970s British family car made by Austin, much mocked for its quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austin Allegro is a discontinued car model, so it is an old car made by that firm.

clue.text: Ultimately fixes electric power tools, getting messy hands

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: the final letters of the three words
awls are pointed tools for piercing holes

explanation.surface: Someone repairing electric power tools ends up with dirty hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' means handwriting, as in a clear hand, and 'messy' describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrawls are untidy, careless pieces of handwriting, and hand is an old word for a style of writing.

clue.text: Son, Charles, 6 stops avoiding work

indicators.note: stops means plugs or blocks, so the number fills a gap inside the royal word

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
Charles III is the British king
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A son, Charles, makes several stops while dodging his duties.
explanation.walkthrough: The 6 looks like a reference to 6 down but is simply the number, in Roman numerals. Skiving is British slang for shirking.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiving is British slang for dodging work or school, so avoiding duty on purpose.

clue.text: Sailor holding up both ends of smoked fish

indicators.note: in a down entry, holding up means sitting underneath and supporting what comes above

blocks.note: read literally: the two ends of the word smoked are S and D, written out with the word and between them
AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor serves up smoked fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'both ends' is taken literally as S AND D, with the joining word kept.
explanation.definitionFit: The sand dab is a small flatfish of the Pacific coast, so an example of a fish.

clue.text: State, say, Ross King’s content to start

indicators.note: the content of a word is what lies inside it, its middle letters
to start puts these letters at the front of the answer

blocks.note: the inside of the word with its outer letters removed
Diana Ross is a singer, so Ross is an example of a surname going with Diana

explanation.surface: A US state is named, and the presenter Ross King is pleased to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: Ross King looks like one man's name but splits: Ross points to Diana Ross, and King gives its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: See 13
Perhaps Best Actress Award – to Screen Guild – occasionally related to kissing

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only alternate letters are kept
to screen is to shield or enclose, so the award surrounds the kept letters

blocks.note: the Oscar is the Academy Award given for Best Actress among others
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: An Academy Award for acting going to the Screen Actors Guild, now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on Screen makes it look like part of a union's name, but it is the verb meaning to hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscular is an adjective from Latin osculum, a little mouth or kiss, meaning concerning the act of kissing.

clue.text: Definitely working out with Bond

indicators.note: working means being processed or kneaded, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is certainly exercising with James Bond.
explanation.definitionFit: No doubt is an adverbial phrase meaning certainly, beyond question, a synonym for definitely.

clue.text: Greek character taken aback by foreign china showing taste

indicators.note: taken aback means pushed backwards, so the letter's name is read in reverse

blocks.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), and ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A Greek man is shocked by a foreign piece of porcelain displaying refined taste.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, so china means friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Umami is the savoury fifth basic taste, alongside sweet, sour, salty and bitter.

clue.text: Watching as, finally, The Big Yin enters

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of each of the words after it
enters means goes into, so the nickname word is placed inside

blocks.note: the last letters of the two words
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fans look on as the comedian Billy Connolly, The Big Yin, comes on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The Big Yin, Scots for the big one, is the nickname of the Glasgow comedian Billy Connolly.
explanation.definitionFit: Eying is a spelling of eyeing, looking at closely, so a synonym for watching.

clue.text: Broad primarily attacks wicket, always keeping eye on the ball

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: broad means wide
the initial letters of the five words

explanation.surface: England bowler Stuart Broad attacks the wicket while always watching the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuart Broad is a famous English cricket fast bowler, so the surface is pure cricket; the definition is just the last three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide awake means fully alert and attentive, which is what being on the ball means as an idiom.

clue.text: Picture of chicken sandwich

blocks.note: chicken and yellow both mean cowardly
a submarine is a long filled roll, a sub

explanation.surface: A photograph of a chicken sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: Picture means film here, and chicken is the adjective for cowardly, not the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow Submarine is the 1968 animated Beatles film, and picture is an old word for a movie.
